full_judgment:
2. It appears that apart from the illegality of registering a document in the absence of its executant when such execution is denied by the executant, the courts below considered that the Miscellaneous Case before the Registering Officer having been disposed of during the War of Liberation and Independence of Bangladesh in 1971 ex parte in the absence of the Executant, it was hit by the provisions of President's Order No. 12 of 1972. In order to assist the Court on the question whether the Registering Officer under the Registration Act is a Tribunal and proceeding taken there under ex-parte is a Legal Proceeding within the meaning of P.O. 12 of 1972, the Deputy Attorney General (Civil) of the Government of Bangladesh was directed to appear before this Court So far as the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General is concerned, he has expressed his views that the Registering Officer while registering a document under the Registration Act is an administrative Tribunal acting in a question judicial manner according to law and consequently the proceeding taken before it, though not a Judicial proceeding, but is a Legal Proceeding and as such the provisions of P.O. 12 of 1972 are attracted thereto. 

 4. The next question for decision is whether the provisions of President's Order No. 12 of 1972 are attracted with regard to a proceeding taken before a Registering Officer under the Registration Act Article 3 of President's Order 12/72 says that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being enforced, all orders passed ex-parte by any Tribunal in legal proceeding at any time after the month of 1st March, 1971 before 7th February, 1972 are hereby declared null and void and the proceedings shall continue in accordance with law. The question is whether the expression-"Tribunal" and "Legal Proceeding" mentioned in Article 3 of the President's Order No. 12 of 1972 include is Registering Officer under the Registration Act and the proceeding taken thereto with reference to section 75 thereof. The expression-"Tribunal" has not been defined in President Order No.12 of 1972 but "Legal Proceeding" has been defined in Article 2 thereof as inclusive of any case. For this purpose apart from the reference to various provisions in Part-VI of the Registration Act between sections 32, 33, 34 and 35, further reference may be made to the provisions of Part-XII of the Registration Act between sections 71, 72, 73, 75, 76 and 77 of the Registration Act. Section 71 of the Registration Act provides for recording reasons for refusal to register any document. Section 72 provides for appeals to the Registrar from orders of Sub-Registrar refusing registration on the ground other than denial of execution. Section 73 provides of application to Registrar where Sub-Registrar refuses to register on ground of denial of execution. Section 74 provides for the procedures to be taken before the Registrar on applications filed before it under sections 72 and 73. Section 75 provides for the procedure for the registrar in case registration is directed. Section 76 provides for refusing registration by the Registrar. Section 77 of the Registration Act finally provides for the institution of a suit before an appropriate court in case of any refusal to register any document by the Registrar under the Registration Act. In this connection particular reference may also be made to Sub-section (4) of section 75 of the Registration Act which says that the Registrar may for the purpose of any enquiry. summon and enforce the attendance of witnesses and compel them to give evidence as if he were a Civil Court and he may also direct by whom the costs of any such enquiry shall be paid and recovered as if they had been awarded in a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure. In view of the aforesaid particular provision in section 75(4) of the Registration Act, the Registrar is undoubtedly an administrative Tribunal required to act in a quasi-judicial manner according to law and the proceeding taken before it though is not a judicial proceeding as such but a legal proceeding Considering the provisions of Part-X II between Sections 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76 and 77 along with Part-VI between Sections 32, 33, 34 and 35 of the Registration Act, it clearly and unmistakenably appears that the entire proceeding before any Registering Officer including an Registrar or Sub-Register under the Registration Act Is a "Legal Proceeding" though not a judicial proceeding and. as such the Registering Officer discharging administrative functions in a quasi-judicial manner according to law after hearing all the relevant interested parties concerned in the registration of any document is a "Tribunal". 

 7. Before concluding it must however be observed that in view of the finding of this Court that the registration of the document in question being made illegally in the absence if its Executant when be bad earlier denied such execution of the document and in view of setting aside of such ex-parte proceeding before the Registrar, the entire matter is liable to be re-opened before the Registering Officer denovo and the Registering Officer may, after considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the provisions of law laid down hereinbefore, dispose of the matter in the manner it deems fit and proper. In this connection reference may also be made to the concluding sentences of Article 3 of President's Order 12 of 1972 that upon declaring of an ex-parte legal proceeding taken before any Tribunal as null and void, such proceeding shall continue in accordance with law as a fresh proceeding.
